1.explanation:
• tree/index.md: Describes the Tree API, including the OnSelect event and the extra.selected parameter which is at the core of this bug.
• tree/adaptor/index.jsx: Contains the React adaptor implementation for Tree, showing how selectedKeys and extra are passed through and where the toggle logic lives.
• tree/demo/basic.md: Provides a minimal working example of Tree selection; useful to compare controlled vs uncontrolled behavior.
• tree/demo/control-select.md: Demonstrates using Tree in a controlled select mode, directly relevant to the user’s use of OnSelect and selectedKeys.
• tree/demo/data.md: Shows loading nodes dynamically and the interplay between data updates and selection state—important for reproducing the user’s data-driven scenario.
• tree/theme/index.jsx: Defines the CSS classes applied for selected nodes; understanding how the selected style is applied helps diagnose why the node isn’t re-highlighting on re-select.
1.bug_scenario: In the user’s page, they render a Tree component on the left and a data table on the right. They’ve wired the Tree’s OnSelect event to a custom handler (onCategoryTreeNodeSelect) that receives two parameters: selectedKeys and an extra object with a boolean field selected. On the first click of a node, extra.selected is true and their state.selectedCategoryId updates accordingly. On the second click the same node, extra.selected flips to false and they clear selectedCategoryId. However on all subsequent clicks of that same node, extra.selected remains false and never returns to true, and the node’s highlight style never toggles back on. Visually the node stays unselected, and they cannot re-select it without refreshing. The expected behavior is that each click should toggle extra.selected between true and false for the same node and visually update its CSS highlight.
